---
title: "1 · Mathematical Foundations"
---

Before we can average over random quantum evolutions, we need a shared
vocabulary: how to describe **quantum channels**, the **Lie-algebraic** structure
that governs how operators grow, the **geometry** of the space of states, and
just enough **measure theory** to make the phrase "a uniformly random unitary"
mean something precise. None of this assumes prior exposure to Lie groups — the
machinery is built up from commutators and the matrix exponential.

Three threads run through the chapter:

- **States and channels.** Density matrices, Kraus operators, and the
  Choi–Jamiołkowski isomorphism that turns a channel into a state.
- **Symmetry and operator growth.** The Lie algebras $\mathfrak{u}(D)$ and
  $\mathfrak{su}(D)$, dynamical Lie algebras, and Schur–Weyl duality — the reason
  random-unitary averages collapse onto a handful of permutations.
- **Geometry and measure.** The Fubini–Study metric, curvature and the quantum
  speed limit, and the measure-theoretic foundation of the Haar measure used in
  every later chapter.

## Notebooks in this part

- [Bloch-sphere geodesics & the Fubini–Study metric](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_fubini_study.ipynb) — the natural distance between pure states.
- [Entanglement of a parametric two-qubit state](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_entanglement_parametric.ipynb) — how entanglement tracks a tunable coupling.
- [The depolarizing channel](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_depolarizing_channel.ipynb) — Kraus operators, complete positivity, and entanglement fidelity.
- [Dynamical Lie algebra closure](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_dla_closure.ipynb) — building an algebra by repeated commutators, and what makes a gate set universal.
- [Schur–Weyl duality for $k=2$](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_schur_weyl.ipynb) — the symmetric/antisymmetric split and the SWAP operator.
- [Choi matrix of amplitude damping](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_choi_amplitude_damping.ipynb) — channels as states via Choi–Jamiołkowski.
- [Dimension of $\mathfrak{u}(D)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(D)$](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_dim_lie_algebra.ipynb) — counting generators.
- [Surjectivity of the exponential map](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_exp_surjectivity.ipynb) — why every unitary is an exponential.
- [Haar invariance on $U(1)$](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_haar_measure_unitary_group_rank_one.ipynb) — what "uniformly random unitary" means, in the simplest case.
- [Geodesic length & the quantum speed limit](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_quantum_speed_limit.ipynb) — how fast a state can change.
- [Sectional curvature of $SU(2)$](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_sectional_curvature.ipynb) — why nearby evolutions reconverge.
- [Differential geometry of state space](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_differential_geometry_hilbert_space.ipynb) — the quantum geometric tensor, Berry curvature, and the Fubini–Study metric together.
- [Measure-theory basics](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_measure_theory_basics.ipynb) — Lebesgue vs counting measure and $\sigma$-additivity.
- [Borel $\sigma$-algebras & measurability on $U(D)$](../notebooks/ch1/solution_ch1_borel_measurability.ipynb) — making "random" rigorous.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**Where to start.** If you only want the tools used later, do *Schur–Weyl
duality*, *Haar invariance*, and *the depolarizing channel* first — everything in
Chapter 3 builds directly on them.
:::
